summary: PSC-NoGate (Predictive Self-Correction without oscillatory gating) achieves 76.4% bit accuracy on the copy task using only local eligibility traces and output error feedback--significantly outperforming both Feedback Alignment (50.8%, near-random) and the oscillatory-gated PSC variant (51.7%)--demonstrating that biologically-plausible temporal credit assignment is feasible without backpropagation. However, a substantial performance gap remains compared to BPTT (100%), and surprisingly, the oscillatory phase-gating mechanism intended to improve biological realism actually *hurts* learning by restricting plasticity to ~50% of timesteps, cutting the effective learning signal in half.
